title: Console API: expose rollout auto-actions (pause/rollback/suppress) with pagination + time filtering
author: Chloe Martin
description:
This PR adds read APIs in console-backend for rollout auto-actions (auto-pause/auto-rollback/suppression/override) so Console can render an audit timeline and oncall can query events without digging through raw event-stream logs. The endpoints support cursor pagination and filtering by rollout_id + time window, and intentionally expose only the fields required by the Console UI and runbooks.

Context
- Rollout controller emits structured audit events for auto decisions (see ADR-0128 and follow-up emitter work in pr-28435).
- Console needs a stable, paginated API to power the rollout timeline + event detail panel (DES-944) and to support oncall queries during incidents.

What’s included
- New endpoints (console-backend)
  - GET /console/api/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/auto-actions
    - Query params: limit (default 50, max 200), cursor, start_time, end_time
    - Sort: created_at DESC, tie-breaker id DESC for stable pagination
  - GET /console/api/v1/auto-actions
    - Query params: rollout_id (required), limit/cursor/start_time/end_time
    - This is primarily for internal tools and admin screens where the rollout id is known but the route is not.
- Response model: AutoActionEvent
  - id, rollout_id, created_at
  - action (PAUSE | ROLLBACK | SHIFT_TO_BASELINE | SUPPRESS | OVERRIDE)
  - outcome (EXECUTED | NOOP | FAILED | SUPPRESSED)
  - reason_code (SLO_BREACH_FAST_BURN | SLO_BREACH_SLOW_BURN | MONITOR_STALE | MIN_SAMPLE_NOT_MET | MANUAL_SUPPRESSION | KNOWN_INCIDENT | POLICY_GUARDRAIL)
  - policy_version + policy_hash
  - monitor_refs (string list of monitor ids, as recorded)
  - metrics_snapshot_ref (opaque pointer; Console links out to Grafana using this)
  - correlation_id (ties back to rollout controller logs)
  - actor (service name; typically rollout-controller) + actor_type (SYSTEM | ADMIN)
  - message (short human-readable summary intended for UI display)
- Data source
  - Reads from the existing audit-events store (backed by the event-stream consumer) using a new query path optimized for (rollout_id, created_at) access.
  - Adds an index/migration for audit_event.rollout_id + created_at.
- RBAC / permissions
  - Requires Rollouts.Read to list events.
  - Fields that expose admin identity / justification (actor_type=ADMIN, message with justification) are only returned for users with Rollouts.Admin (INT-8832 follow-up will add the explicit permission name in the admin bundle; for now it maps to existing "console_admin" group).
  - Endpoints are tenant-scoped; rollout_id must belong to the requester’s org.
- Pagination semantics
  - Cursor is an opaque base64 token containing (created_at, id) of the last item.
  - start_time/end_time are inclusive bounds; server enforces max range of 30d to protect the audit store.

Not included
- Write APIs (suppression/override). Those are tracked separately and will land with the admin override PR (pr-28511).
- Search by route/model/region. We can add once the UI + policy model stabilizes; keeping scope tight for MVP.

Testing
- Unit tests for query bounds, cursor decoding/encoding, ordering stability, and RBAC redaction.
- Integration test against a local audit-event store fixture verifying pagination over ties and correct filtering by time window.

Operational notes
- These endpoints are used by Console UI only when the auto-rollback feature flag is enabled.
- Added basic request metrics (latency + 5xx) and a log line with rollout_id and cursor for debugging.

Rollout plan
- Land behind existing Console feature flag "rollouts_auto_actions".
- Enable in staging once pr-28435 (emitter) is deployed and audit events are flowing.

Screens / examples
- Example: GET /console/api/v1/rollouts/rlt_2mV5n8K/auto-actions?limit=2&start_time=2026-02-10T00:00:00Z
  - returns two most recent events + next_cursor for fetching older items.

Follow-ups
- Wire Console timeline UI (ENG-4833).
- Add dashboards/alerts for missing/stale monitors (ENG-4840).
commits: console-backend: add AutoActionEvent API model + DTO mapping
audit-store: add query helper for (rollout_id, created_at) with cursor pagination
authz: enforce Rollouts.Read and redact admin-only fields without Rollouts.Admin
db: add index on audit_event(rollout_id, created_at, id)
tests: pagination stability + bounds + redaction coverage
docs: add internal API notes for rollouts auto-actions endpoints
review_conversation: Felix Schneider: Can we guarantee stable pagination if multiple events share the same created_at? Also would be good to include correlation_id for linking back to rollout-controller logs.
Chloe Martin (author): Yep — cursor encodes (created_at, id) and ordering is created_at DESC, id DESC. Added correlation_id to the response model + mapping (see commit 3f2c8b1).
Hannah Rivera: For the UI we’ll need a single human-readable message string so we don’t have to re-implement reason code formatting in TS. Can we add that server-side and keep it short?
Chloe Martin (author): Added message with a canonical formatter (action + reason + outcome). It’s intentionally brief and stable; UI can still show reason_code as a tag if desired.

Kevin Osei: RBAC: returning admin justification to all Rollouts.Read users is a compliance risk. Please ensure redaction unless the user has explicit admin permission. Also confirm tenant scoping on rollout_id lookup.

Chloe Martin (author): Done — admin-only fields are redacted unless Rollouts.Admin (currently mapped to console_admin). Added tests for both roles. Tenant scoping enforced by org_id join on rollout lookup.
Allison Grant: Metric labels — please avoid adding rollout_id as a label on request metrics (cardinality).
Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. No rollout_id labels; only route name + status_code class. Added rollout_id only to structured logs.
Felix Schneider: Approved after last push. This unblocks ENG-4833 UI work.
Kevin Osei: Approved (with the redaction tests).
release_notes: Console backend now exposes read-only endpoints to list rollout auto-actions (pause/rollback/suppress) with cursor pagination and time filtering, including RBAC-based redaction for admin-only details.
